🧪 Tested in Patagonia & Norway
9.0

Holiday Video Camera Rating

6K video, phase-detect autofocus, and dual native ISO. The best full-frame hybrid for serious travel filmmakers.

The Panasonic Lumix S5 II finally fixes Panasonic's autofocus weakness with phase-detection. Combined with 6K video, dual native ISO, and a compact full-frame body, it's a travel filmmaker's dream.

Key Specifications

Sensor24MP Full-Frame
Video6K30, 4K60 (unlimited)
AutofocusPhase + Contrast detect
Stabilization5-axis in-body
Dual ISOISO 640 / 4000
Price$1,699 (body)

🎬 6K Video Quality

The 6K30 footage is incredibly detailed with 14+ stops of dynamic range. In Patagonia's high-contrast landscapes, I recovered shadow detail in glaciers while preserving highlight detail in bright skies.

🎯 Phase-Detect Autofocus

Panasonic's DFD autofocus was always the weak point. The S5 II adds phase-detection, and the difference is night and day. Eye-tracking is now competitive with Sony and Canon.

🌙 Dual Native ISO

Dual native ISO (640 and 4000) means clean footage in almost any lighting. In Norway's Northern Lights, ISO 4000 produced usable footage with minimal noise.

❌ Trade-offs

  • Heavier than APS-C competitors
  • L-mount lens selection is growing but limited
  • No 4K120 (only 1080p120)
  • Price puts it in professional territory
💡 Best Lens: The Lumix S 20-60mm f/3.5-5.6 kit lens is surprisingly sharp and compact. Perfect for travel.
